reason: grep_check_excl pipes grep -hiE into grep -viE. On a file that holds a NUL byte the first grep prints only a 'binary file matches' notice, to stderr since grep 3.5 (to stdout before, which makes the helper answer TRUE). With grep 3.11 the helper therefore answers FALSE for any file with a NUL, whatever it contains: the four exclusion rules are blind to such a file.
decision: Accepted divergence, in the safe direction: rx.search_excl(binary='text') examines the file (like grep -a); binary='grep' reproduces bash for the differential run. Report the blind spot to the lead as a bash gap.

reason: Once grep decides a file is binary (a NUL byte) it treats the NUL as a line end, so ^ and . behave differently around it; with -I it skips the file. rx.search_lines has binary='text' (default, grep -a), 'grep' (NUL ends a line) and 'skip' (grep -I). rx decides for the whole file at once; grep decides as it reads, so a NUL that first appears late in a large file would affect only the lines after it. That is not modelled.
decision: Accepted: the engine uses 'text' unless a differential test needs 'grep'. Verified against grep for the three modes on crafted files.

reason: grep_flat tests wc -c <= 5242880 and otherwise returns 1 (no match): a larger file is skipped, not cut, with no message. The three XXE rules (and any future flat rule) are therefore blind to an XML file over 5 MB. The task text said 'cut at the cap'; the bash does not cut.
decision: rx.flat_view / search_flat reproduce bash (b'' over the cap). Report to the lead as a bash gap; the Python engine should add a reported WARN (inspection_incomplete) when it skips.

reason: bash runs grep in the caller's locale; rx is the C locale (one byte, one character, ASCII case folding). Measured with pattern_fuzz.py --locale C.utf8: 0 of 294 patterns differ from rx on 29,287 real repository lines (they include non-ASCII text), but 146 differ on generated lines that contain invalid UTF-8, where a UTF-8 grep refuses to let . and [^x] match the bad byte or treats the line as binary.
decision: Accepted: C-locale byte semantics are the documented contract. Run the bash oracle with LC_ALL=C in the conformance harness.

reason: grep returns the leftmost-longest match, re the leftmost-first. For 'does the line match' this cannot matter. For grep -o (4 direct sites, 1 BRE/ERE pair and the 18 credential patterns) the matched text can differ with an ambiguous alternation.
decision: Accepted: rx.only_matching is leftmost-first. The gate compares the matched text with grep -o on all of those patterns (about 22,000 tokens) and finds no difference, because none of them has an ambiguous alternation.

reason: The only back-reference in the pipeline is in KNOWN_CRED_EXCL (([A-Za-z0-9])\1{9,}). A back-reference has no DFA, so that pattern cannot use the budget= fallback.
decision: Accepted: it runs on the text of one matched token (under 300 bytes), never on a file line, so it cannot be driven quadratic.

reason: rx refuses (UnsupportedERE) constructs on which grep's own two matchers disagree: [.x.] and [=x=], a '{' at the start of an expression, an interval or an anchor after a repetition operator that has nothing to repeat, a repeated anchor next to a back-reference, a back-reference to a group that can be empty or is repeated, newline-separated patterns with a back-reference. None occurs in the 294 pipeline patterns.
decision: Accepted: refuse loudly at compile time instead of choosing an answer.

reason: Two behaviours depend on the grep version: the 'binary file matches' notice (stdout before 3.5, stderr after), which flips grep_check_excl on a binary file, and the warnings for stray backslashes (3.8+). Measurements here are GNU grep 3.11.
decision: Accepted: the gate prints the grep version it ran against; re-run it when the oracle's grep changes.
